parts:
Hi all,
I have tried to declare the Wheaton indicators as ordered factor variables. I have used the ordered argument from the second option I have read in http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html. I think that I have failed in something because the output includes the ML estimator that assumes continuous data. Below is the syntax and the output.

library(lavaan)
lower <- '
11.8336
6.947424 9.3636
6.819456 5.091228 12.5316
4.782976 5.028192 7.494888 9.9856
-3.83904 -3.88926 -3.8409 -3.62452 9.61
-21.89904 -18.830628 -21.784452 -18.775456 35.52228 450.2884'

wheaton.cov <- 
    getCov(lower, names = c("anomia67", "powerless67", "anomia71", "powerless71", "education", "sei"))

wheaton.model <- '
    ses     =~ education + sei
    alien67 =~ anomia67 + powerless67
    alien71 =~ anomia71 + powerless71
    alien71 ~ alien67 + ses
    alien67 ~ ses
'

fit <- sem(wheaton.model, sample.cov = wheaton.cov, sample.nobs = 932, ordered=c("anomia67", "powerless67", "anomia71", "powerless71", "education", "sei"))
summary(fit, standardized = T, fit.measures = T)
inspect(fit, "sampstat")$cov

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Wheaton classic data as ordered factors
parts: the output includes the ML estimator that assumes continuous data.

I think that is because you have only provided a covariance matrix as data.  When data are ordinal, the polychoric correlation matrix must be estimated from the contingency table.  You should provide the raw data to lavaan, which it will use to estimate thresholds and polychoric correlations.  This document provides technical information about categorical CFA:

http://www.statmodel.com/examples/webnote.shtml#web4

Terry
